using AI outputs and AI-assisted decisions

objective: Make LSE staff and students aware of the legal and regulatory issues around AI use (competition and confidentiality, copyright, cybersecurity, data protection, equality) so that they do not breach the law when using AI.

related_policies.policy: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/lse-legreg.pdf). The document is labelled 'Operational' and version 2, approved by the AI Working Group on 24/10/2024 (PDF created Dec 2024); its next review was due 31/10/2025, so a newer version may exist. Classed as guidance/voluntary because it is framed as guidance, although it says it sets out 'the guidelines you must operate under' and breaches (e.g. of confidentiality) may lead to disciplinary sanctions. No official LSE URL is printed in the document. The legislation section (EU AI Act, UK AI Regulation Bill, TUC manifesto) reflects the position as at June 2024.

clauses.original_text: Don’t put personal data in an AI tool that is external to LSE. If it will swallow the personal data for further processing that LSE cannot control, you can’t use the AI tool.
clauses.requirement: do not enter personal data into external AI tools whose further processing LSE cannot control
clauses.condition: where the AI tool is external to LSE
clauses.purpose: UK GDPR compliance; prevent loss of control over personal data
clauses.affected_asset: personal data of staff, students and research subjects
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Phrased as a 'Don't' instruction in the guidance; repeated in the Cybersecurity AI rules ('do not ingest any personal data into AI tools') and Data Protection principles ('Do not share personal data with external AI tools').

clauses.original_text: Don’t upload in-copyright content (for example , images, photographs, student work, journal articles licensed from publishers by LSE library) where you do not have the copyright holder’s permission and where the AI tool is known to use inputs as training data.
clauses.object: in-copyright content (images, photographs, student work, licensed journal articles)
clauses.recipient: AI tools that use inputs as training data
clauses.requirement: do not upload copyrighted material without permission to tools that train on inputs
clauses.condition: where the copyright holder has not given permission and the tool is known to train on inputs
clauses.purpose: avoid copyright infringement and breach of library licences
clauses.affected_asset: third-party copyright works; LSE library licences
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Stray space before the comma ('for example , images') is in the source. The Copyright section adds that MS Copilot may be used to summarise copyrighted work and that the TDM exception (s.29A CDPA) covers only non-commercial research.

clauses.original_text: Conduct an Equality Impact Assessment if there is a chance of data leading to bias or discrimination.
clauses.actor: LSE staff and students using AI
clauses.requirement: carry out an EIA where AI use could lead to bias or discrimination
clauses.condition: if there is a chance of data leading to bias or discrimination
clauses.purpose: comply with the Equality Act 2010; prevent discrimination on protected characteristics
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Listed under 'Do'; imperative but the document is guidance. The Equality Act section elaborates (profiling, automated decision-making, EIAs).

clauses.original_text: Remember that you're always accountable for any decisions you make, so be very wary of making decisions solely based on AI outputs. Any automated decisions that have real-world impacts on humans must allow for a human review.
clauses.object: automated decisions with real-world impacts on humans
clauses.requirement: automated decisions affecting people must allow human review; users remain accountable for decisions
clauses.condition: where automated decisions have real-world impacts on humans
clauses.purpose: accountability; UK GDPR Article 22 safeguards against solely automated decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Linked to the Data Protection section's discussion of UK GDPR Article 22 (e.g. students told if AI is used for marking and able to request human review).

clauses.original_text: Do not trust any information supplied by AI tools without undertaking independent verification. AI tools are known to hallucinate, namely supplying information that has no basis in reality, or else reproducing information that is out of date or is misinformation.
clauses.requirement: do not rely on AI-supplied information without independent verification
clauses.purpose: avoid reliance on hallucinated, outdated or false information
clauses.affected_asset: accuracy of work products and decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)

clauses.original_text: Never ask an AI to perform tasks that are malicious or that may compromise other people or data that is not yours. This at a minimum would constitute a breach of the Computer Misuse Act 1990, the Terms of Use of Jisc’s network, our M365 tenancy agreement and the standard terms of most AI tool providers.
clauses.object: malicious tasks or tasks compromising other people or their data
clauses.requirement: no malicious use of AI or use that compromises others' systems or data
clauses.purpose: prevent computer misuse and harm to third parties
clauses.affected_asset: other people; third-party data and systems
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Echoes 'Don't ask an AI tool to do something malicious or illegal' under 'What not to do'.
